newsitem.title: TURKEY: Nadir's ex-wife convicted for buying stolen Koran.
newsitem.headline: Nadir's ex-wife convicted for buying stolen Koran.

text.p: A Turkish court has sentenced the former wife of fugitive tycoon Asil Nadir to four and a half years in jail for buying a stolen antique Koran, a court official said on Wednesday.
"She was given a jail sentence of four years and six months for buying stolen goods," a court official in the northern Turkish town of Amasya told Reuters.
He did not give further details on Tuesday's verdict.
Aysegul Nadir, known by her maiden name of Tecimer, had only attended the trial's first hearing in 1994 and according to Turkish newspapers recently went to live in Miami in the United States.

She twice married and divorced Turkish Cypriot businessman Asil Nadir, who jumped bail and fled from Britain to northern Cyprus in 1993 after the collapse of his London-based Polly Peck business empire. He had been awaiting trial on theft and false accounting charges.

The Amasya court gave two men 12-year jail sentences for stealing the hand-written Koran and Tecimer, an Istanbul socialite and expert on Islamic art, was convicted for buying the book and selling it for $15,000.
In 1996, a Turkish court gave her a 10-month suspended jail sentence for hoarding hundreds of antiques illegally in her mansion by Istanbul's Bosphorus Straits.
